messages:
Rafael: Morning! I'm finishing my first-week notes and want to make a shared "team playbook" in Notion. Two quick asks: (1) where does Redwood prefer these living docs to live so teammates can edit without me emailing every change, and (2) can we have an automated backup to our Git repo via the Notion API?
Maya (DevEx): welcome Rafa :wave: For collaboration put playbooks in Docs > eng > <team-name> (not your private space). That way the space-level group permission (eng@redwood.com or <team>@redwood.com) controls edit rights.
Jordan: seconding Maya. Also we usually add a page property `doc_kind` = "playbook" and `owner` = <team> so Ops can filter.
Rafael: got it. I tried to move my page but Notion says "You don't have permission to move this page". It was generated from the public template gallery.
Maya (DevEx): common. If a template originated in another team's space you'll need Docs Ops to transfer it (to preserve comments/history) or the owner can grant you Duplicate rights. Want us to open a ticket?
Rafael: yes please open a ticket. Also curious about the Git sync idea.
Docs Admin: filing DOC-1102: "Transfer & promote: Rafael playbook -> eng/<team>". Assignee: Docs Ops. link: https://tickets.redwood.com/DOC-1102
notion-bot: DOC-1102 created by Docs Admin. Status: Open.
Jordan: about backups -> we don't store secrets in Notion. If you want content in Git we usually add a CI job that fetches the public parts via Notion API and commits to the docs repo. That requires a read-only Notion integration token and a service account. Ping infra for token provisioning.
Rafael: who's allowed to create a Notion integration? I don't want to accidentally create a token that has too much scope.
Maya (DevEx): only Docs Ops can create org-level integrations. Individual users can create page-level integrations but they expire/are scoped. For repo-sync we recommend Docs Ops create a scoped read-only integration and add it to the target page. Open DOC-1103 if you want Docs Ops to set it up.
Docs Admin: added DOC-1103: "Notion -> Git sync: request for eng/<team> (read-only integration)". https://tickets.redwood.com/DOC-1103
Rafael: perfect, thanks. Another slightly different question: how do we handle templates that are team-specific vs org-wide? I made a small onboarding checklist and wonder if it belongs in Templates or under our team space.
Jordan: team-specific small checklists live under your team space (Docs > eng > <team> > onboarding). Org-wide templates go into Docs > Templates > Team templates and follow the naming convention `tpl-<area>-<short>` (eg `tpl-onboard-check`).
Maya (DevEx): to promote a team doc to org template: duplicate it, move duplicate to Docs > Templates > Drafts, add `template_status` = "candidate" page property, then open a PR in the Templates tracker (link on the Templates page). Docs Ops/Design will review before we mark `template_status` = "approved".
Rafael: nice. Any naming or sorting rules I should follow for the page title so it appears in the space nav?
Jordan: prefixing with numbers for ordering is common, like `01-onboard`, `02-runbook`. Use lowercase, hyphen-separated.
Rafael: one last nit: are there any groups besides eng@redwood.com we should use for editors? I see `eng-oncall@` and some other aliases.
Maya (DevEx): eng@redwood.com is the default for read/write across engineering. Use team-specific groups (<team>@redwood.com) when you want to limit edits. eng-oncall@ is for rota/alerts and not for doc perms. If you're unsure, mention the group in the Docs Ops ticket and we'll validate.
Rafael: thanks all, closing the loop. When DOC-1102/DOC-1103 are done I'll update the playbook and promote it to Templates if it's generic. Appreciate the fast help :tada:
